title: The shared HTTP server stops on Windows while a client holds an idle connection
goal: On shutdown the shared HTTP transport closes idle connections by shutting their sockets down from the stopping thread. On Windows that does not wake a recv that is already blocked, so a connection waiting between requests stayed until its client closed it and serve() never returned: stopping the daemon could hang for as long as any client kept a keep-alive connection open. On Windows an idle connection now waits for its next request in 100 ms timed peeks and checks the stop flag between them. Other hosts are unchanged.
validation: On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: server::tests::shutdown_finishes_the_request_in_flight_and_closes_idle_connections failed 3 of 3 runs before (serve() did not return within 5 s) and susi-http-transport passes 48 of 48 in 3 of 3 runs after; clippy -p susi-http-transport --all-targets -D warnings clean. The change is cfg(windows), so Linux builds the same code as before; not run on Linux.
limitations: A stopping server is noticed by an idle connection within 100 ms, not at once.
A TLS connection that has received part of a record when the server stops still waits for the rest of that record.
